name: Northern Quadra Island clam gardens
description: Indigenous communities managed clam habitat with rock-walled intertidal terraces on northern Quadra Island, according to archaeological and community evidence.

impact.note: Communities on one island built terraces to farm clams; a new ability locally, with descent of other coastal clam gardens from here not shown.

date.label: About 3500 calibrated years before 1950
date.basis: The date is scoped to this described observation, text, archaeological interpretation or object, not the origin of the wider practice.

events.statement: Indigenous communities managed clam habitat with rock-walled intertidal terraces on northern Quadra Island, according to archaeological and community evidence.

evidence.supports: The researchers, including First Nations coauthors, used dated samples and relative sea-level reconstructions to infer that clam gardens at northern Quadra Island existed about 3500 years ago. Shell persistence, later wall building and changing sea levels complicate construction dates. Kee k us (Elizabeth Harry) told a historian in 1993 of maintaining a Waiatt Bay wall during her lifetime.

events.caveats: The approximate age is an interpretation combining shell samples, relative sea level and wall elevations, not direct dating of the walls or a universal origin date. Old-shell effects and later modification can complicate individual garden chronologies. The island is within traditional territories of Laich-Kwil-Tach and northern Coast Salish peoples; a specific ancient wall cannot be attributed to a named individual. The same study notes earlier optically stimulated luminescence dates of about 1,200–1,900 years for two deposits, substantially younger than its radiocarbon/sea-level interpretation; the authors identify methodological uncertainty.
